All tests pass. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed:

**Problem:** Claude Code agent only implemented `HookResponseWriter` (outputs `systemMessage` shown to the user), not `HookContextWriter`. When `explanatory_insights.live_injection` was enabled, the code in `writeSessionStartHookResponse()` fell through to the fallback path that combined the prompt into the visible `systemMessage` — so the user just saw the raw prompt text printed, instead of it being injected into the model's context.

**Fix:** Added `HookContextWriter` implementation to the Claude Code agent (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/lifecycle.go`):
- Added `WriteHookResponseWithContext(message, additionalContext)` method
- Refactored `WriteHookResponse` to share a common `writeHookResponse` helper
- The JSON response now uses `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` to inject the prompt into Claude's context window (same pattern Codex and Gemini CLI already use)
- Added compile-time interface assertion

Now when `live_injection` is enabled, the explanatory insights prompt will be injected via `additionalContext` into the model, while the session banner remains the only visible message to the user.

97		if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(cmd.Context()); err != nil {

99		}
100	
101		// Skip if Entire is not enabled
102		enabled, err := IsEnabled(cmd.Context())
103		if err == nil && !enabled {
104			return nil
105		}
106	
107		if initLogging {
108			cleanup := initHookLogging(cmd.Context())
109			defer cleanup()
110		}
111	
112		// Initialize logging context with agent name
113		ctx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(cmd.Context(), "hooks"), agentName)
114	
115		// Strategy name for logging
116		strategyName := strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit
117	
118		hookType := getHookType(hookName)
119	
120		// Start root perf span — child spans in lifecycle handlers and strategy
121		// methods will automatically nest under this span.

123			slog.String("hook_type", hookType))
124		defer span.End()
125	
126		logging.Debug(ctx, "hook invoked",
127			slog.String("hook", hookName),
128			slog.String("hook_type", hookType),
129			slog.String("strategy", strategyName),
130		)
131	
132		// Set the current hook agent so handlers can retrieve it
133		currentHookAgentName = agentName
134		defer func() { currentHookAgentName = "" }()

136		// Use the lifecycle dispatcher for all hooks
137		var hookErr error

139		if agentErr != nil {

141		}
142	
143		handler, ok := agent.AsHookSupport(ag)
144		if !ok {

146		}
147	
148		// Use cmd.InOrStdin() to support testing with cmd.SetIn()
149		event, parseErr := handler.ParseHookEvent(ctx, hookName, cmd.InOrStdin())
150		if parseErr != nil {
151			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook event: %w", parseErr)
152		}
153	
154		if event != nil {
155			// Lifecycle event — use the generic dispatcher
156			hookErr = DispatchLifecycleEvent(ctx, ag, event)
157		} else if agentName == agent.AgentNameClaudeCode && hookName == claudecode.HookNamePostTodo {

159			hookErr = handleClaudeCodePostTodo(ctx)

---

**What changed:**

The explanatory insights feature was moved from being inline logic in the lifecycle dispatcher to a **standalone Claude Code hook**, similar to the [explanatory-output-style plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/explanatory-output-style).

1. **`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/hooks.go`** — New hook name `explanatory-insights`. `InstallHooks()` conditionally installs/removes it based on the `live_injection` setting. Added `removeSpecificHookCommand` helper.
